high.title: VN-Index Loses Over 100 Points in a Single Week: What Awaits Investors?
high.summary:
The Vietnamese equity market suffered one of its sharpest weekly corrections since the start of 2026. The VN-Index shed approximately 120 points in just the first three sessions of the week, with the most severe single-day drop of over 62 points occurring on July 22nd, decisively breaching the psychologically critical 1,700-point support level. Large-cap stocks led the selloff, with many hitting daily price limits. Modest dip-buying emerged in the final sessions, but sellers consistently re-emerged near the 1,700 level, capping any recovery. The index ultimately closed the week at **1,686.1 points, down 101.3 points (-5.6%)**, marking the **fourth consecutive week of losses**. The HNX-Index declined 18.7 points (-6.4%) to 272.9. Notably, weekly turnover surged over 23% versus the prior week — but this reflected panic selling and forced liquidations rather than fresh institutional inflows. **Key implication:** The structural breakdown below 1,700 signals deteriorating market sentiment. Foreign fund managers should monitor whether this triggers further capital outflows from Vietnamese equities, which could add depreciation pressure on VND. Watch the 1,650 level as the next technical support.

---

high.title: "Horrible July": Billion-Dollar Foreign Fund Manager's View on Vietnam's Stock Market in July
high.summary:
Pyn Elite Fund — one of the most prominent foreign funds with dedicated exposure to Vietnamese equities — reported a **-9.6% return in July** (through July 22), while the **VN-Index collapsed -10.3%** over the same period. Fund manager Petri Deryng described July as the worst performing month since inception and the heaviest loss month since October 2023, labeling it "Horrible July" in his investor letter.

Deryng expressed surprise at the severity of the sell-off, particularly given strong Q1 earnings growth from listed companies and Vietnam's robust H1 macroeconomic performance. He attributes part of the weakness to elevated investor caution, which amplified the downward price momentum.

medium.title: Taiwan's Fubon FTSE Vietnam ETF Returns to Net Buying After 165 Days — A Potential Inflection Signal for Foreign Capital Flows
medium.summary: After more than five months of continuous net outflows or zero transactions, Taiwan's Fubon FTSE Vietnam ETF recorded its first net inflow on July 23, 2026 — the first since February 9, 2026, marking a 165-day gap. The fund issued a net 2.5 million units, equivalent to approximately TWD 44 million (~VND 36 billion) deployed into Vietnamese equities. While the absolute size is modest, the directional change is notable. Fubon FTSE Vietnam ETF is one of the largest foreign ETFs invested in Vietnam, with total AUM of approximately TWD 10.7 billion (~VND 8,700 billion). The fund tracks Vietnamese equities and has been under sustained redemption pressure alongside broader foreign selling across the market. For FX and equity market participants, a sustained reversal in Fubon's flows would be a meaningful positive signal for USD/VND dynamics, as foreign equity inflows provide a source of USD supply into the Vietnamese market. However, one session does not constitute a trend — fund managers should monitor whether this buying is sustained over the coming weeks before drawing conclusions about a broader re-rating of Vietnam by foreign institutional investors.

medium.title: Wave of Margin Calls Hits Listed Company Executives as Stock Prices Collapse
medium.summary: A wave of forced margin call (giải chấp) liquidations is sweeping across multiple listed Vietnamese companies as the stock market continues to probe multi-year lows. Securities firms have been forcibly selling pledged shares held by company executives and related parties. Notable cases include: FPT Securities (FPTS) liquidating 128,400 shares of textile company TCM belonging to a board member when the stock fell to VND 17,300 — its lowest level since November 2020; and three sessions of forced selling at real estate developer Hodeco (HDC). This margin call wave is symptomatic of broader market stress and is relevant for bond and FX investors as a systemic risk indicator. Sustained forced selling by insiders can deepen equity market corrections, potentially triggering broader risk-off sentiment, reducing domestic liquidity, and adding pressure on the VN-Index. If margin call activity escalates to the banking sector or systemically important names, it could have downstream implications for banking sector asset quality and credit conditions — a key watchpoint for government bond yield dynamics.

medium.title: Should You Buy Certificates of Deposit for Higher Interest Rates?
medium.summary: This advisory piece highlights that Vietnamese banks are currently offering certificates of deposit (CDs) at notably attractive interest rates — particularly for longer tenors — as banks compete for stable, term funding. CDs differ from standard savings deposits in that they carry fixed maturities and typically do not permit early redemption or offer it only under restrictive conditions. The article implicitly signals that deposit rates remain elevated, consistent with a higher-cost funding environment across the banking sector. **Relevance for bond and FX traders:** Elevated CD rates reflect sustained upward pressure on the banking system's cost of funds, which could compress net interest margins for lenders and delay any meaningful easing in lending rates. This also suggests the SBV has not yet shifted toward an accommodative stance, which is a headwind for Vietnamese government bond prices and supports a higher-for-longer yield environment. Investors should watch whether competition for deposits intensifies further, as this would be a leading indicator of liquidity tightness in the interbank market.

medium.title: Fundamentally Strong Stocks FPT, MWG, SSI All Down Double-Digits Year-to-Date — Experts Explain Why
medium.summary: Blue-chip Vietnamese equities including FPT, MWG (Mobile World), SSI, MSN, and VJC have all declined by double-digit percentages since the start of 2026, with FPT falling to its lowest price level in nearly three years (since early November 2023). Industry expert Bui Van Huy (CEO of FDIT) attributes this to valuation de-rating driven by rising interest rates — a dynamic that disproportionately impacts high-multiple growth stocks, as higher discount rates compress the present value of future earnings. He notes that stocks previously rewarded with premium valuations for long-term growth narratives are now facing the steepest multiple compression. **Key implication for fund managers:** This analysis confirms that the equity market correction is fundamentally rate-driven, not purely sentiment-based. Rising borrowing costs and deposit rates are systematically repricing Vietnamese equities. Until there is a credible signal from the SBV that a rate-cutting cycle is imminent, premium-valued growth stocks remain vulnerable. This also reinforces caution on the broader VN-Index outlook.

medium.title: Q2 2026 Financial Results Update (Morning of July 27): One Bank Reports a Loss
medium.summary: Saigonbank reported a pre-tax loss of VND 40 billion in Q2 2026, a stark reversal from a VND 76.4 billion profit in the same period last year. For H1 2026, Saigonbank's cumulative pre-tax profit totaled only VND 48 billion, down 72.4% year-on-year — underscoring significant stress in the smaller bank segment. Meanwhile, Eximbank's acting CEO disclosed at an extraordinary shareholder meeting on July 24th that H1 2026 pre-tax profit is estimated at VND 730 billion, representing only 48% of the full-year target and a 51% decline year-on-year. **Relevance:** Deteriorating bank profitability — particularly among mid-tier and smaller banks — is a key risk factor for the broader financial system. Weakening earnings increase the probability of asset quality deterioration and could prompt the SBV to reassess its regulatory stance. For VND and bond traders, banking sector stress typically signals tighter credit conditions and potential systemic risk premium expansion.

medium.title: A Stock "Hits the Floor" for 11 Consecutive Sessions — What Is Happening?
medium.summary:
ACC shares (Binh Duong ACC Investment & Construction JSC, listed on HoSE) have hit the lower circuit limit for 11 consecutive sessions since July 13, with the stock price collapsing to VND 4,850/share — the lowest level since 2020 — down from a long-standing range of VND 12,000–14,000. HoSE has issued two formal explanation requests to the company covering the periods July 13–17 and July 20–24. The company attributed the sell-off to pure supply-demand dynamics and investor sentiment, offering no fundamental explanation. While ACC is a small-cap construction name with limited systemic significance, the episode is a marginal signal of broader market stress on HoSE. International fund managers should note: prolonged lower-circuit events can indicate liquidity fragility in mid/small-cap segments of the VN-Index, and repeated HoSE inquiry letters may reflect heightened regulatory scrutiny of unusual price movements in the current environment.

---

medium.title: Securities Brokerage Revenue Dries Up: Structural Pressures Mount in Q2 2026
medium.summary: Vietnam's securities brokerage sector posted its weakest quarterly performance since Q1 2025, with industry-wide brokerage revenue falling 27% quarter-on-quarter and 5% year-on-year to approximately VND 3,600 billion in Q2 2026 — less than half the ~VND 7,000 billion peak recorded in Q3 2025. More alarmingly, gross profit collapsed by over 63% QoQ and 50% YoY to roughly VND 400 billion, as cost reductions failed to keep pace with revenue deterioration. Gross margin compressed sharply to ~11%, down from 22% in Q1 2026 and 21% in Q2 2025 — one of the lowest readings since 2023. The article attributes the weakness not only to poor market liquidity but also to structural shifts in brokerage business models. For VN-Index watchers, this is a meaningful negative signal: declining brokerage profitability reflects reduced retail participation and thinner trading volumes, which can weigh on market sentiment and liquidity. Watch for whether Q3 2026 shows any recovery in turnover as a leading indicator for broader equity market health.

medium.title: Vietnam's Neighbor China Imports 173 Tonnes of Gold in June — Highest in Over Two Years
medium.summary: Chinese customs data show gold imports surged to approximately 173 tonnes in June 2026, up from 163 tonnes in May and marking the third consecutive monthly increase — the highest monthly import figure since March 2024. The article attributes the acceleration to a combination of lower gold prices attracting dip-buyers, a stronger CNY improving domestic purchasing power, and Chinese commercial banks restocking physical gold inventories to meet retail demand including gold accumulation programs. While this is a China-focused story, it carries indirect relevance for Vietnam: sustained Chinese gold demand keeps global gold prices elevated, which historically amplifies domestic Vietnamese gold price premiums and pressure on the SBV to manage the gold market. Elevated domestic gold prices in Vietnam have in the past contributed to USD/VND volatility as informal gold-dollar arbitrage flows emerge. Monitor SBV's gold import quota policy and any divergence between domestic and international gold prices as a secondary FX risk indicator.

medium.title: H1 2026 Banking Sector Results: 15 Banks Update — VIB, VietABank, VPBank, Techcombank and Others
medium.summary: A broad H1 2026 earnings update across 15 Vietnamese commercial banks reveals a mixed but broadly stable picture for the sector. VIB posted pre-tax profit of VND 5,180 billion (+3% YoY), with total assets exceeding VND 580 trillion (+4% YTD), credit growth of +4%, and customer deposits up +8%. VietABank delivered stronger momentum with pre-tax profit of VND 826 billion (+15.7% YoY), total assets of VND 149 trillion (+11.3%), and loan growth of +10%. Most notably, Saigonbank swung to a pre-tax loss of VND 40 billion in Q2 2026 (vs. a profit of VND 76.4 billion in Q2 2025), with cumulative H1 profit collapsing 72.4% YoY to just VND 48 billion — a red flag for asset quality at smaller lenders. For bond and FX investors, the divergence between large private banks (healthy growth) and smaller institutions (liquidity stress) warrants monitoring, as it could influence SBV's appetite for further easing and its approach to system liquidity management in H2 2026.

medium.title: Unprecedented Wave: Over 30 Gold, Silver, and Diamond Businesses in Ho Chi Minh City Close Down
medium.summary: According to the Chairman of the Ho Chi Minh City Gold, Silver & Gemstone Craft Association, more than 30 gold, diamond, and precious stone businesses in HCMC have suspended operations since early July 2026 — an unprecedented development. The primary causes cited are deteriorating business conditions, mounting cash flow pressure, and a surge in customers selling jewelry back to dealers, overwhelming dealers' liquidity capacity. The actual number of closures is likely higher as many non-member businesses have not been captured in the survey. Several prominent gold and diamond brands — including Kim Ly, Ngoc Chau Au, and Ngoc Tam — have previously come under regulatory scrutiny. While this is a retail-sector story, the sharp contraction in the domestic gold trade is a marginal negative signal for consumer confidence and may reflect broader liquidity stress among Vietnamese households — a factor worth monitoring alongside VND stability and gold price dynamics.

medium.title: Evening Gold Prices on July 26: SJC Bar Gold and Ring Gold at SJC, PNJ, DOJI, Bao Tin Minh Chau and Bao Tin Manh Hai
medium.summary: Domestic gold prices closed flat on July 26 after a sharp weekly decline, with no intraday movement recorded. SJC bar gold closed at VND 137.5–141.5 million/tael (buy/sell), down VND 6–7 million/tael versus the prior week-end. PNJ, DOJI, Bao Tin Minh Chau, and Bao Tin Manh Hai posted identical or near-identical levels. Ring gold (vàng nhẫn) also fell sharply on the week, with SJC closing at VND 137–141 million/tael, down VND 5.5–6 million/tael. The magnitude of the weekly decline — roughly 4–5% — is significant and likely reflects the recent pullback in international gold prices. For VND/FX watchers, softer domestic gold prices reduce speculative demand for USD to fund gold imports and may marginally ease pressure on the SBV's FX intervention posture.

medium.title: H1 2026 Results of 13 Banks: 3 Names Show Negative Growth, One Bank's Profit Jumps 5x
medium.summary: A clear divergence is emerging across Vietnamese banking sector profitability in H1 2026. Saigonbank reported a pre-tax loss of VND 40 billion in Q2 2026 (vs. a profit of VND 76.4 billion in Q2 2025), with cumulative H1 pre-tax profit collapsing 72.4% year-on-year to just VND 48 billion. Customer deposits at Saigonbank fell 4.26% from year-start, a potential signal of funding pressure. Eximbank fared worse on a relative basis — H1 pre-tax profit of approximately VND 730 billion represents a 51% year-on-year decline, completing only 48% of its full-year target. Total assets reached VND 266,500 billion at end-Q2. For bond and FX market participants, deteriorating bank profitability — particularly at smaller and mid-tier lenders — raises questions about credit quality, potential non-performing loan (NPL) buildup, and whether the State Bank of Vietnam (SBV) may face pressure to maintain accommodative monetary conditions to support the banking system. Watch for any SBV guidance on NPL provisioning or capital adequacy requirements in coming weeks.
